- scripts/activation_verify.sh:line 121 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The linked issue number is interpolated into a `gh api` URL without validation at the interpolation site.
  WHY: The upstream numeric regex validation means no actual injection path exists.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:line 416-421 | severity=low | confidence=[1]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The fetched `head_sha` is interpolated into a `gh api` URL.
  WHY: The value is strictly validated as a 40-character hexadecimal SHA before use, so there is no injection risk.
- scripts/unblock_actions.py:line 238 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The auto-answer comment posts model text after `/answer` without stripping leading slash commands.
  WHY: The current handler treats the remainder as answer text, but a future handler matching midline commands could interpret model output as a tracking-issue command.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:lines 447-453 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The terminal close path may pass a multiline reason into the verdict JSON.
  WHY: Quoted `jq --arg` handling and later `_clean_text` normalization prevent shell injection and normalize text before posting.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:lines 20601-20609, 20639-20647 | severity=low | confidence=[1]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: `unblock_handover_merge_deferral` interpolates the PR number into API calls.
  WHY: The function validates the PR number at entry, and `gh` form fields encode the label and comment body.
- scripts/unblock_scan.py:lines 197-198 | severity=low | confidence=[1]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: A busy-item number could cause the scan to skip both an issue and a PR with the same number.
  WHY: GitHub uses a unified numbering namespace, so the two item kinds cannot share a repository number.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:lines 383-388 | severity=low | confidence=[1]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The judge does not re-read item state after refreshing the wait marker and before posting its verdict.
  WHY: The reviewer considers the race benign because the poller processes the shared comment stream in order.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:line 424 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: Failed evidence generation falls back to the same `{"reason": "unreadable"}` evidence for distinct items.
  WHY: Identical fallback evidence produces a shared fingerprint, so one verdict can prevent separate treatment of other unreadable items and waste verdict budget.
- scripts/unblock_ledger.py:lines 303-308 | severity=low | confidence=[1]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: Marker deduplication combines item markers and project markers when counting rounds.
  WHY: The deduplication key includes the item, and the reviewer concludes the item and project round counts are correct.
- scripts/unblock_scan.py:line 226 | severity=low | confidence=[1]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: Sorting candidates would fail if a candidate's `since` value were `None`.
  WHY: The earlier guard excludes candidates with `since is None` before sorting.
- scripts/unblock_actions.py:lines 258-261 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: `_approve` continues adding labels and posting `/approved` even if removing `ai:destructive-blocked` fails.
  WHY: The issue can retain `ai:destructive-blocked` alongside `ai:awaiting-approval`, which causes implement.yml to reject it and leaves it stuck until manual label cleanup.
- .github/ai/label_contract.v1.json:lines 212-218 | severity=low | confidence=[1]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The new labels may not exist in consumer repos until label synchronization runs.
  WHY: The reviewer considers on-demand label creation through `label_helpers.sh` consistent with existing practice.
- .github/workflows/issue_pr_status.yml:lines 718-845 | severity=low | confidence=[1]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: No implicit execution risk was found in the new `activation-verify` job.
  WHY: It runs post-merge, fails open, has a kill switch, and removes credentials from the model environment.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml:lines 1229-1317 | severity=low | confidence=[1]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: No implicit execution risk was found in the new standalone auto-decide step.
  WHY: It is bounded, uses existing answer-posting logic, and excludes orchestrator-managed and force-reclarified issues.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:handle_unblock_judge_project_hooks, lines 15804-15808 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The fix-up request regex captures `item` and the item number embedded in `id` independently without checking that they agree.
  WHY: A mismatched trusted comment could associate the fix-up issue with one item while its wave key references another; normal `unblock_judge.sh` output is consistent, so this is a defense-in-depth gap.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:lines 15779-15808 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: A fix-up issue is recorded in `issue_number_map` but not appended to any wave when the wave array is empty or `wave_idx` is out of bounds.
  WHY: The wave iterator will not pick up the fix-up issue, so the project may not progress and the orphaned fix-up can be lost.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:unblock_main, unblock_run_ops auto_decision branch, lines 226-241 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: A bot identity change can cause the auto-decision renderer to create a second auto-decision comment rather than update the prior bot's comment.
  WHY: Both bot identities may be trusted, and the renderer may not treat the older bot comment as authoritative.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:551-563 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: If `render_prompt.sh` fails, the fallback passes the raw template, including unrendered Jinja include tags, to the model.
  WHY: The model then receives the role description without the rendered system prelude.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:unblock_ask_model, lines 565-589 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: A `write_codex_config.sh` failure silently skips the Codex call.
  WHY: The judge can post an `invalid_verdict` wait marker and exit successfully, masking the persistent configuration failure until the next retry.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:unblock_run_ops, add_labels case (lines ~210-217) | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `unblock_judge.sh` does not source `label_helpers.sh`, so `ensure_label_exists` is undefined and the add-label operation uses the GitHub API directly.
  WHY: Adding a label that does not yet exist can fail silently, leaving the poller unable to see `ai:unblock-closed` and repeatedly dispatching the judge.
- .github/workflows/unblock_judge_dispatch.yml, .github/workflows/unblock_judge.yml:unblock_judge_dispatch.yml lines 30-31 (`jobs: judge: uses: ...@main`), unblock_judge.yml "Judge the blocked item" step | severity=low | confidence=[1]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: No implicit execution gap was found in the unblock judge dispatch or reusable workflow.
  WHY: The dispatch is gated by the enable flag and scan rate limits, and the reviewer reports those controls are documented.
